title: Give each headless role the permissions its actual job needs, not this repo's

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL — round 1. Audited e3bd25e with bookkeeping 8e27b81, main checkout. Sprint file read fresh. Working tree clean apart from the known .vscode file.

The FAIL trigger did not fire — no profile is repo-specific any more, and I proved that rather than reading it. Two findings, and an answer to your question at the end.

================================================================
THE FAIL TRIGGER — CHECKED FIRST, AND THE SWEEP IS LOAD-BEARING
================================================================

"A profile that only works in this repository is a FAIL." No profile does. The two repo-specific entries are gone from all three roles that carried them (`Bash(node scripts/launcher_test.js)`, `Bash(bash scripts/verify-tarball.sh)`), and what remains — `scripts/run-lifecycle.js` and `scripts/sprint_lifecycle.py` — is framework-owned and installed into every target, so those paths exist wherever the framework does. Verified against a real installed target rather than assumed.

Req 5's criterion says to confirm the sweep actually fails against the current definitions, so I falsified it rather than running it: reintroduced `Bash(bash scripts/verify-tarball.sh)` into pipeman's list and re-ran the suite.
    FAIL run-role: no role's static allowedTools hardcodes a path specific to this repository (Req 5)
It bites. Restored, suite clean. That test is the one the sprint file named as what would have caught this class, and it would.

REQ 2 — MET, and checked against the case the criterion names. The new statement is "`acceptEdits` governs TOOL use (Edit, Write). It says nothing about Bash. Every Bash command, including git, needs its own `--allowedTools` entry or it isn't approved — full stop." Tested against sprint 12's finding as instructed: a plain Bash redirect writing while Edit/Write are disallowed is the same boundary seen from the other side, and the new wording covers both directions explicitly rather than only the one this sprint hit. It would have prevented the earlier defect, which is the criterion's actual test.

REQ 1, DEV-TEAM MECHANISM — MET, read cold. `needsTestCommand` plus a declared `fullyCompletely.testCommand`, no default and no grant when undeclared, is the right shape: the framework no longer needs to know the target's test runner in advance, and an undeclared command fails closed rather than falling back to something. That is the half of Req 1 that could most easily have been solved by hardcoding a better guess.

REQ 4 — 0.1.17. REQ 5 — 143 OK, ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED; ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED; verify-tarball.sh PASSED, "Installed 0.1.17 (first install)".

================================================================
FINDING 1 (blocking) — PIPEMAN CAN NO LONGER RUN ITS OWN DOCUMENTED PRE-PUBLISH STEP
================================================================

Removing `Bash(bash scripts/verify-tarball.sh)` was CORRECT and I want that on the record before the finding: `verify-tarball.sh` is not in FRAMEWORK_OWNED and does not land in an installed target — I checked a real one, the file is absent. Keeping it would have been the exact FAIL this sprint exists to prevent.

But pipeman.md step 9.1 still says, unconditionally, as part of every package release:
    "**Run `scripts/verify-tarball.sh` first**, with step 8's state-file write from a moment ago still
     sitting uncommitted in your working tree."
So the role's stated capability and its allowlist now disagree, which is precisely what Req 1's criterion asks me to check role by role ("confirm the stated capability matches the allowlist"). A headless Pipeman releasing THIS project cannot perform its own documented step 9.1 — it will hit an unanswerable permission request and stop. Legible rather than silent, which is the good version of this, but it is a capability this sprint removed without reconciling the instruction that depends on it.

There is a second-order problem underneath, worth naming because it is the same class one level up: pipeman.md instructs running a script that exists only in this repository. That is a repo-specific instruction in an agent file that ships to every target, which is this sprint's own defect in a different artifact.

REQUIRED FIX, and it is a decision rather than a mechanical edit:
  EITHER ship verify-tarball.sh (add it to FRAMEWORK_OWNED) and allowlist it for pipeman, which makes
  both the instruction and the profile correct everywhere;
  OR condition step 9.1 on the script existing, marking it a framework-development step rather than a
  target-project one, and leave the profile as it is.
I have no preference. What should not survive is a documented step the role is not permitted to take.

================================================================
FINDING 2 (blocking, and it is Req 3 applied consistently) — THE NARROWNESS STANDARD WAS APPLIED TO git AND NOT TO npm/npx
================================================================

Req 3's criterion: "Confirm each widening is the narrowest form that does the job. `Bash(git *)` where `Bash(git push *)` would do is a finding, not a convenience."

git is exemplary. Ten enumerated subcommands, each justified against a specific pipeman.md step — status/log/diff/fetch for branch review at step 2, add/commit for 9.3 and conflict resolution, rebase/merge for step 5, checkout for step 4, push for 6 and 9.3. That is the standard the criterion is asking for and it is met precisely.

npm and npx are not held to it. Pipeman and LiveQA both get blanket `Bash(npm *)`; LiveQA also gets blanket `Bash(npx *)`. The comment records that they were TESTED, which is true and good, but records no argument for why they cannot be enumerated the way git was — and the tested cases are narrow ones: `npm publish --dry-run`, `npm view`, `npm --version`, `npx <published package>`.

The grants are strictly broader than what was carefully avoided for git:
  - `Bash(npm *)` includes `npm install`, which executes arbitrary postinstall scripts from the
    registry, in an unattended role, in whatever directory it was launched in.
  - `Bash(npx *)` executes any package on the registry.
Both exceed `git push` in reach, and `git push` is the one the sprint went to ten lines of trouble not to grant broadly.

REQUIRED FIX: apply your own git standard to npm. Pipeman's documented job needs publish, view and pack — `Bash(npm publish *)`, `Bash(npm view *)`, `Bash(npm pack *)` enumerate exactly as cleanly as the git list does. LiveQA's npm use is `npm view`; enumerate it.
`Bash(npx *)` is the one I would NOT insist on narrowing: LiveQA's job is running a published package whose name varies by project, so the pattern may be genuinely irreducible. If that is the reasoning, state it — an argued-for broad grant is a decision, an unargued one is the thing Req 3 exists to catch. Right now it reads as the latter only because nothing says otherwise.

================================================================
YOUR QUESTION — THE git push NON-REPRODUCTION
================================================================

Short answer: it does not change how I weigh Req 1's pipeman criterion, and yes, it is worth its own follow-up — a bigger one than you framed it as.

WHY IT DOES NOT CHANGE THE VERDICT ON THE FIX. The criterion asks whether the stated capability matches the allowlist. Pipeman's job includes pushing; the allowlist now names `Bash(git push *)`. That is correct whether or not the old profile happened to work, and it is correct under both observed behaviours. Allowlisting something you rely on is right even when it currently appears to be granted implicitly — especially then. Your reasoning for applying it anyway ("explicit beats implicit, especially given the CLI already changed once mid-investigation") is the right call and I would have pushed for it if you had not made it.

Reporting the non-reproduction instead of quietly building on the Context's claim is the correct handling, and it is worth saying that plainly: three sprints ago this project shipped a comment asserting something a run would have disproven. This is the opposite, and the difference is that you ran it.

WHY THE FOLLOW-UP IS BIGGER THAN pipeman's git ENTRY. The thing that no longer reproduces was established by running, on a real machine, and recorded as CONFIRMED. It is not wrong-by-carelessness; it is wrong-by-drift. And it is not alone: `docs/sprint-12-permission-scope-findings.md` is this project's reference for every permission decision since, and I grepped it — it records no `claude` version anywhere. Its CONFIRMED entries include exactly the class of finding that just moved: "git push (including to a real remote) is allowed under acceptEdits", "npm is blocked even for `npm --version`". The CLI is now 2.1.261; sprint 14 recorded a different one.

So the follow-up is not "recheck git push." It is: every CONFIRMED in that document has an unrecorded version dependency, and one of them has already expired. The cheap fix is to stamp the CLI version into the findings document and into any future permission finding, so the next drift is detectable rather than discovered by accident three sprints later. That is Master Controller's to scope, and it is the more valuable half of what you found.

================================================================
INFORMATIONAL
================================================================

1. You could not test `--bare` (no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), and noted an unattended orchestrator would more
   likely use it. Agreed, and worth carrying: the non-reproduction is established for the operator-session
   path only. That is a real limit on the finding, correctly stated rather than glossed.
2. Carried, unchanged: the --agents argv budget against Windows' 32,767-char limit; the interactive
   auth-check ordering from sprint 11 round 1.

RECOMMENDATION

Two fixes, one commit: reconcile pipeman.md step 9.1 with the profile (either direction), and enumerate npm the way git was enumerated — with npx either narrowed or argued for. Then round 2 is short; I have no other open items and everything else is verified.

Flag the CLI-version-drift item to Master Controller separately. It is not this sprint's to fix and it is the most consequential thing this sprint turned up.
